summary: L-4 cab built on Bearhead Mountain in 1931, removed or destroyed in 1957 (sources differ); a rusted pipe stub is the only remnant a source describes.

facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1957 (sources differ on the wording); the hiking guide says little evidence remains, a rusted pipe nub among the rocks

staffing.status: lookout camp in 1929; Jess Rose named as lookout in 1929 and 1930; cabin manned until 1957 per the hiking guide

access.note: Summit reached on Bearhead Mountain Trail #1179.1, a six-mile hike; the hiking guide says a Northwest Forest Pass is required. No closure found in the pages read

visit.trail_note: No tower remains. The hiking guide describes a summit hike with views of Mt. Rainier. It starts at the end of FR 7810, which runs 6.5 unpaved miles from the turn just before the Carbon River Ranger Station, then follows Summit Lake Trail #1177, Carbon River Trail #1179 and Bearhead Mountain Trail #1179.1.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest per firelookout.com)

events.note: Lookout camp on the summit; Jess Rose was the lookout in 1929 and 1930 (WillhiteWeb)
L-4 cab built at the summit in 1931
Panoramic photos taken from the summit on August 1, 1934
Register, hiking guide and Washington lookouts list say the cab was removed in 1957
firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say the cab was destroyed in 1957
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on May 22, 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, the hiking guide and the Washington lookouts list say the cab was removed in 1957. firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say it was destroyed in 1957. All sources agree on the year, so both wordings are recorded as events and the story says the sources disagree.

notes_for_editor: Brief county (Pierce) and elevation were not confirmed in the pages read. The 1957 removal versus destruction wording conflicts across sources. The hiking guide is the only source for remains today, and it is a secondary blog. No Forest Service page for the summit was found. Summit access is an inference from the hiking guide.
